title: No Stove, No Frying: Four Diwali Sweets Ready in 15 Minutes or Less
excerpt: Coconut ladoos in 10 minutes, a date and dry-fruit roll, chocolate biscuit truffles and microwave pedas — no-cook recipes for a Diwali party table when the kitchen is already full.
body:
• Four Diwali sweets can be made with no frying and almost no cooking: coconut ladoos (10 minutes), a date and dry-fruit roll, chocolate biscuit truffles and milk-powder pedas (15 minutes each).
  • Every recipe is built on condensed milk or dates as the binder — no sugar syrup, no string-consistency judgement calls.
  • The date roll and coconut ladoos keep well chilled, so they can be made a day ahead of a party.
  • Full ingredients and method for the coconut ladoos are in the recipe card with this article.

Diwali party cooking usually fails in the same place: too many dishes, one stove, and guests arriving before the frying is done. The way out is to take sweets off the stove entirely. The no-bake recipes gathered by IndulgExpress deliver rich festive flavours in 10 to 15 minutes each, without standing over hot oil.

The four to make

Instant coconut condensed milk ladoos (10 minutes). Mix two cups of desiccated coconut with one cup of sweetened condensed milk and half a teaspoon of cardamom powder until a dough forms. Roll into balls, coat in more desiccated coconut and top with sliced pistachios. That is the entire method.

Date and dry fruit roll (15 minutes). Pulse seedless dates to a paste, warm a teaspoon of ghee in a pan with chopped mixed nuts — cashews, almonds, walnuts — and the date paste for three to four minutes until sticky. Shape into a log, roll in toasted poppy seeds, chill in the freezer for 10 minutes and slice into rounds. It looks like a mithai-shop burfi and contains no added sugar beyond the dates.

Chocolate biscuit truffles (15 minutes). Crush Marie or digestive biscuits to a fine powder, mix in two tablespoons of cocoa powder and enough condensed milk to bind, shape into balls and dip in melted dark or milk chocolate. Set on parchment paper.

Quick milk powder peda (15 minutes). Microwave one tablespoon of ghee, one cup of milk powder, half a cup of condensed milk and two tablespoons of saffron milk for two minutes, stirring every 30 seconds. Cool slightly, knead smooth, shape into small discs and press a pistachio into the centre of each.

Why no-cook works for Diwali specifically

Cookpad's fireless Diwali collection makes the same argument from the host's side: skipping frying removes the splatter, the oil and the last-minute workload, and make-ahead sweets free the day itself for savouries and guests. Condensed-milk-based sweets also travel well — a box of coconut ladoos survives a drive across town to a friend's Diwali party in a way a syrup-soaked sweet does not.

Two practical notes. The date roll and ladoos firm up in the fridge and slice or serve better after an hour chilled, so make them first. And because none of these recipes involves a sugar syrup, they are forgiving for first-time mithai makers — there is no one-string or two-string consistency to miss.
